messages:
Kasia: hit a weird issue this morning when running a bunch of localtest workers. redwoodctl login keep retrying aggressively and one of our auth providers started returning 429 with Retry-After. CLI ignores Retry-After and keeps hammering, which made the provider blacklist the CI IP for a few minutes.

Ben: ouch. does redwoodctl use exponential backoff today? i thought it did but maybe not honoring headers.

Kasia: it has a simple retry loop with fixed sleep (2s) and max 5 attempts for device code flows. code snippet from our binary: 
```go
for i:=0;i<5;i++ {
  resp, _ := pollDeviceCode()
  if resp.Status==200 { saveToken(); return }
  time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
}
```
No handling of 429 or Retry-After.

Hao: that will definitely cause problems under parallel seeds. provider recommends honoring Retry-After and using jittered exponential backoff. Also we should detect 429 and return a specific exit code so callers can treat it as a transient throttle.

Ben: agreed. short-term mitigation: add a guard in sample-app seed to avoid parallel headless logins (flock) and backoff on 429. Long-term: make redwoodctl: 
- respect Retry-After header when present
- switch to exponential backoff with jitter (e.g., base=1s, max=60s, jitter=uniform)
- return exit code 72 for throttle so scripts can retry with backoff
- add telemetry counters for 429s so we can alert when clients hit provider limits

Kasia: i prototyped a small change: 
```go
if resp.Status==429 {
  wait := parseRetryAfter(resp)
  time.Sleep(wait + jitter())
  continue
}
// else exponential backoff
```
Works locally.

Hao: also consider adding a client-side circuit-breaker for repeated 429s per profile so local dev doesn't keep retrying for minutes. e.g., after 3 429s within 1m, fail-fast with a clear message: "Auth service throttled requests; try again in Xs or use --ci-token".

Ben: good idea. and update quickstart docs to recommend `flock` pattern for docker-compose seed and show using `--ci-token` environment variable to skip login when running many parallel workers.

Kasia: filed issue #4120: "redwoodctl: honor Retry-After and exponential backoff for headless/device login; return throttle exit code" and assigned to @hao. devex-bot created the issue :spiral_note_pad:

ops-bot: scheduled CI job `devex/auth-backoff` to run on hao/auth-backoff branch

Hao: i'll send a small PR: 1) parse Retry-After, 2) add jittered backoff, 3) circuit-breaker counter scoped to REDWOOD_HOME, and 4) tests mocking 429 + Retry-After. Will also add a short note in onboarding about running parallel logins.

Ben: thanks — can you include a changelog note that CLI now returns a specific exit code for throttles so integrators can react?

Kasia: thanks everyone — that should stop our CI from getting blacklisted. :thumbsup:
